fatal_errors: The proposed post-quench annealing is not the target intervention, which was compositional adjustment to Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 combined with melt spinning at 40 m/s.
The hypothesis assumes a usable Tg and a sub-Tg annealing window, whereas no glass transition was detected for the target ribbon, so Tg-based treatment cannot be specified from the reported data.
The expected Tx range of 960–1290 K is incompatible with the target ribbon, whose crystallization began near 659 K and was complete near 820 K.
Post-quench relaxation cannot explain or overcome primary crystallization during solidification because it is applied only after a fully amorphous ribbon has already been produced.
Evidence E2 concerns an unspecified, different metallic glass and does not establish a glass-to-glass transition or a 50–100 K stabilization in this Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni–P alloy.
A reduced DSC exotherm after annealing is not uniquely evidence of greater amorphous stability; it may indicate partial crystallization during the anneal.
explanation: The response addresses amorphous retention and proposes a testable treatment-control comparison, but it does not reconstruct the reported solution. The paper altered Fe/Co/Mn ratios and reduced phosphorus from 20 to 15 at.% to suppress primary solid-solution and high-temperature phosphide formation, promote eutectic-dominated solidification, and then used rapid melt spinning to suppress segregation and obtain a fully amorphous approximately 20 μm ribbon. The generated mechanism instead invokes an unverified glass-to-glass relaxation in the original P20 composition. Its thermal boundaries are inconsistent with the reported devitrification range, and the absence of a detected Tg invalidates the stated sub-Tg protocol. The experiment could detect DSC changes, but it should also quantify crystalline fraction before and after annealing; otherwise a lower exotherm could result from annealing-induced crystallization rather than stabilization.
